rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers affirm God's oneness and revelation, worship sincerely, and believe in the afterlife's moral distinctions and recompense.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın birliğini ve indirdiğini tasdik edip O’na ihlâs ile ibadet ve tâate ikrar vermişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith must permeate the believer's faculties and will, producing deeds aligned with belief, God's commands, truth, and good for self and others.
rows.anchor: imanları yalnız gönüllerinde ve dillerinde kalmamış, bütün hislerine, akıllarına, mevcudiyetlerine nüfuz ederek iradelerine sâhip olmuşlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action includes fulfilling duties and avoiding major sins and indecencies; scripture and Sunna detail its foundations, with particulars entrusted to consensus and juristic reasoning.
rows.anchor: emrolunan vazifeleri edâ, nehyolunan kebâir ve fevâhişten ictinab eylemişlerdir ki bunların esası Kitap ve Sünnet’te tafsil olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After faith, righteous action has two kinds: bodily acts that benefit the agent and acts such as alms that benefit others, perfecting self or other.
rows.anchor: Birisi bedenî ibadetler gibi mükellefin evvelen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most important outward good deeds are inviting others to truth and striving in its path.
rows.anchor: Bunun en mühimi de hakka davet ve hak yolunda mücahededir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who counsel one another in truth direct their resolve, faith, deeds, and speech toward truth, since what is not directed to truth is falsehood and loss.
rows.anchor: bütün azimleri hakka müteveccih, imanları da amelleri de kavilleri de hep hakka masruf olmuş; çünkü hakka masruf olmayan her şey bâtıldır, hasardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in truth means doing and uniting upon what is established and right, calling to truth, commanding good, forbidding wrong, and acting uprightly.
rows.anchor: her işte hak, sâbit, doğru olanı yapmayı, hak üzere birleşmeyi, hep hakka davet eylemeyi, emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münkeri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counseling patience is necessary because worldly distractions, desires, and the many who lose make good works and truthful speech painful and demanding.
rows.anchor: hayır yapmak, hak söylemek, hak yolunda gitmek birçok acılar çekmeye, zorluklara katlanmaya, mücahede etmeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman 31:17 explicitly advises those who command right and forbid wrong to bear patiently what befalls them, calling this resolve among great matters.
rows.anchor: diye isabet edecek musibetlere sabır tavsiye edilerek onun azme mütevakkıf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in al-Balad, the fortunate are believers who surmount the steep path and counsel both compassion and patience to one another.
rows.anchor: “akabe”yi iktiham eden ve iman edip de birbirlerine hem merhamet hem sabır tavsiye edenlerin meymenet sâhipleri oldukları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience keeps people from retreating or weakening in difficult trials, and includes mutual support through worship, affliction, and resistance to desire.
rows.anchor: caymamayı, yılmamayı, bıkmamayı, zaaf göstermemeyi ve böylelikle birbirlerini yardımsız, tesellîsiz bırakmayıp gerek tâat ve amel ve gerek âlâm ve mesâib ve gerek şehevâta karşı sabr u metanet tavsiye etmeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is the soul's strength to endure pain and hardship in doing good or avoiding evil; the source distinguishes two principal kinds.
rows.anchor: Mâlum ki sabır nefsin iyi bir iş yapmak veya fenalıklardan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of patience bears the hardship of obedience, striving, and good works, enabling the achievements of people with high aspiration.
rows.anchor: Birisi elem ve külfete sabırdır ki bununla tâat ve mücahedenin ve güzel amellerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another kind resists pleasure and desire, protecting people from forbidden acts and attractive but dangerous harms.
rows.anchor: Birisi de lezzet ve şehevâta karşı sabırdır ki bununla da haramdan, menhiyyâttan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate capacity matters, but training, habit, resolve, will, and especially faith also shape patience.
rows.anchor: fıtrî kābiliyetin bir hükmü bulunduğu münker olmamakla beraber terbiyenin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is commanded as a voluntary duty; believers are told to persevere, outdo others in patience, stand guard, and fear God to prosper.
rows.anchor: sabır, ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyeden olarak ef‘âl-i mükellefîn meyânında tavsiye olunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites God's support and limitless reward for the patient, including praise for those who respond to calamity by affirming their return to God.
rows.anchor: إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadiths describe patience as the key to relief and say that the patient triumphs.
rows.anchor: مَنْ صَبـَرَ ظَفَرَ “sabreden zafer bulur”[^47] diye vârid olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish proverbs likewise call patience the beginning of knowledge and say its end is well-being.
rows.anchor: dilimizde de “ilmin başı sabırdır”, “sabrın sonu selâmettir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised patience is faith-filled perseverance in good work and truth, marked by courage, fidelity, and honor, rather than passive acquiescence to evil or humiliation.
rows.anchor: memduh olan ve tavsiye edilen sabır, iman ve amel-i sâlih ile hak ve hayır yolunda sabırdır ki bu şecaat, sadakat, mertlik şi‘ârıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting evil is itself evil and accepting unbelief is unbelief; patience cannot mean inertia, remaining trapped in wrong, or failing to try to escape degradation.
rows.anchor: şerre rızâ şer, küfre rızâ küfürdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet approved a poet's saying that gentleness without forceful outbursts to protect its purity has no good in it; the poet is not named here.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah beğenmişti: وَلاَ خَيْرَ فِي حِلْمٍ إِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ بَوادِرُ تَحْمِي صَفْوَهُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound hadith commands changing a wrong by hand, then by speech if unable, then by the heart if unable, which is the weakest faith.
rows.anchor: “sizden her kim bir münker, bir biçimsizlik görürse onu eliyle değiştirsin. Ona gücü yetmeyen diliyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an 6:68 and 4:140 instruct believers to leave gatherings where God's signs are mocked, supporting active resistance rather than passive patience.
rows.anchor: فَلَا تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when patience is inappropriate, believers should act with insight rather than panic or rashness, following the prophetic way of calling to God knowingly.
rows.anchor: basîret ile hareket etmelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those with faith, righteous works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience are exceptions to humanity's otherwise absolute loss; all four express complete faith.
rows.anchor: ancak böyle iman, sâlih ameller, tevâsî bi’l-hak, tevâsî bi’s-sabr dört vasıf ile muttasıf olan kimseler hüsranda değil, müstesnâdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True faith in the real and abiding God cannot fail; a life spent in beautiful works for God is never wasted, while faith in falsehood and its deeds vanish.
rows.anchor: O’nun yolunda güzel amellere sarfedilmiş bulunan bir hayat, bir ömür hiçbir zaman boşa gitmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that even people with true faith incur a kind of loss if they do not perform righteous deeds and counsel truth and patience.
rows.anchor: Hakk’a iman etmekle beraber sâlih ameller yapmayan ve hak ve sabır tavsiye etmeyen kimseler de bir nevi hüsrandan hâriç kalmamış olurlar

rows.speaker: Mürcienin
rows.claim: The Murji'a claim that lack of action causes no loss once faith exists is false; Ahl al-Sunna correctly holds that sinful, disobedient believers also incur a kind of loss.
rows.anchor: “iman olunca amelsizlik ziyan etmez” diyen Mürcienin kavilleri hak değildir. Doğrusu ehl-i sünnetin dedikleri gibi imanı olup da imanına göre âmil olmayan fâsıklar, âsîler için de bir nevi hüsran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although faith ultimately saves sinful believers, those whose sins outweigh their good deeds undergo Hell's loss until their sins are cleansed.
rows.anchor: seyyiâtı hasenâtından ağır gelen mü’minler de günahları temizlenene kadar cehennem azâbı olan hüsrânı göreceklerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Medîne
rows.claim: He reports that two of the Prophet's Companions would not part after meeting until they recited Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other and then exchanged greetings.
rows.anchor: Ebû Medîne’den[^57]-ki sohbeti vardır- şöyle dediğini rivayet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author urges his contemporaries to notice time passing, counsel truth and patience, and seek success in good works through complete faith; those who mock such counsel face the severe loss described next.
rows.anchor: birbirlerimize hak ve sabır tavsiye etmeye ve Hak teâlâ’ya îmân-ı kâmil ile güzel amellere muvaffakiyet dilemeye ihtiyâcımız ne kadar çok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa links this description causally or as the answer to an omitted condition; the definite predicate restricts the referent to people who deny judgment.
rows.anchor: Fâ, sebebiyye veya şart-ı mahzûfun cevâbı olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of judgment harshly shoves and drives away the orphan, exploiting the child's weakness without mercy or fear of God.
rows.anchor: insaf ve merhamet etmeyerek kakar kakıştırır, kahr u hakāretle kovar azarlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a person neither feeds the poor himself nor encourages relatives or others able to help to feed them, and shows no concern for the needy.
rows.anchor: sâir kimselerin bakıp gözetmesi, it‘âm etmesi için de kayırmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the food 'the food of the poor' rather than simply 'feeding' hints that the needy person has a religiously recognized right to food held by the able.
rows.anchor: “ta‘âm”dan murad it‘âm olduğu için “it‘âmü’l-miskîn” demek daha zâhir olacak iken “ta‘âm” denilmesi nüktelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor person's entitlement is so strong that feeding them is like paying one's debt and should not be used to shame them.
rows.anchor: öyle bir bîçâreyi doyuran kimse onun kendi hakkı olan bir taâmı vermiş, borcunu ödemiş gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verbs indicate habitual conduct; the surrounding context condemns people who, despite rescue from hunger and fear, fail their duties of worship and mutual care for orphans and the hungry.
rows.anchor: يَدُعُّ، وَلَاَ يَحُضُّ fiilleri istimrar ifade eder muzâri‘olmak hasebiyle bu âyetlerin yukarıya rabtından çıkan mânanın hâsılı şu olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting the orphan and ignoring the poor are habitual traits of those who deny religion; once faith is denied, such cruelty is unsurprising, while its appearance among the devout is more astonishing.
rows.anchor: böyle yetimi kakmak ve fukarâya bakmamak gibi insafsızlıklar dine yalan diyen kimselerin yapageldikleri âdeti, huyu demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning now turns to those who pray or appear to be believers, threatening them with woe for being heedless of their prayers.
rows.anchor: daha doğrusu namaz kılıyor mü’min görünenlere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer should gather the heart before God, bring a kind of meeting with Him, and elicit aid and guidance for sincere service; heedlessness abandons these purposes.
rows.anchor: dinin direği ve kulların cem‘iyyet-i kalb ile huzûr-ı Hakk’a durarak bir yükselişi, likāullâha bir nevi visâli demek olan

rows.speaker: Atâ b. Dînâr
rows.claim: He explains that the verse condemns heedlessness away from prayer, not involuntary mistakes during prayer, which human beings cannot fully avoid.
rows.anchor: Atâ b. Dînâr’dan mervî olduğu üzere denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness includes treating prayer as unimportant, neglecting whether or when it is performed, delaying or abandoning it without regret, praying insincerely for worldly aims, or praying publicly but not privately.
rows.anchor: kılınıp kılınmadığına aldırmamak, vaktine dikkat etmemek, geçip geçmediğine mübâlât etmeyip vaktinden tehir eylemek, terkinden müteessir olmamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness also includes performing prayer as empty display or amusement rather than sincere worship; complete abandonment is outside the address to people who pray.
rows.anchor: Söz musallî denilenlerde olduğu için büsbütün terk bu mevzudan hâriç olmak gerektir

rows.speaker: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkas
rows.claim: He reports asking the Prophet about those heedless of prayer and receiving the explanation that they delay it past its proper time.
rows.anchor: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkas radıyallâhu anh’tan, demiştir ki: “Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ne

rows.speaker: Ebû Berzete’l-Eslemî
rows.claim: He reports that the Prophet called the verse better than receiving the whole world and described people who neither expect reward from their prayer nor fear their Lord when abandoning it.
rows.anchor: Ebû Berzete’l-Eslemî radıyallâhu anh’tan, demiştir ki:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context includes people who perform a few prayers smugly as if religion consisted only of them, neglecting other duties such as almsgiving and help for God's servants.
rows.anchor: kıldıkları birkaç vakit namazdan dolayı mağrur olup yanılıp da din ondan ibaret imiş gibi sâir ibadet ve ubûdiyet vazifelerini yapmayanlar da dâhil olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly pairs prayer with zakat as foundational righteous duties after faith; some who seem devout wrongly neglect financial obligations.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da imandan sonra sâlih amellerin esası olmak üzere namaz ve zekât beraber zikrolunagelmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques are maintained by those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear only God.
rows.anchor: إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing; people who persist in these and refuse aid have ignored prayer's admonition and meaning.
rows.anchor: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites perform deeds for public display and people's approval rather than for God.
rows.anchor: Her ne amel yapsalar Allah için yapmazlar da halka gösteriş için ve herkesin göreceği yerde yaparlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿūn may mean zakat, or even the smallest customary loan or assistance; those who withhold such minor help would all the more withhold zakat.
rows.anchor: mâ‘ûnu men ederler zekâtı vermezler, yahut kimsenin esirgemeyeceği âriyet gibi cüz’î bir yardımlığı bile sakınır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.
rows.anchor: namaz kılar dindar görünüp de namazlarından yanılan, mürâîlik, gösteriş yapıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Māʿūn explains the preceding Sūrat Quraysh; its wording 'woe' and its meaning of withholding aid then connect it to Sūrat al-Humaza.
rows.anchor: Mâ‘ûn Sûresi ile tavzih olunarak buradan “veyl” kelimesi ile lafzen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the address to the Prophet to see and understand, Sūrat al-Kawthar condenses the preceding suras, especially those from al-Ḍuḥā, as a final account of Muhammad's rank.
rows.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelerin mazmûnu üzerinde hepsinin tetimmesi
